arrow_components.answer_anchor_quote: In one line, it's "always be learning."  Where that gets interesting is that by the time a model like Claude ships, it has finished its training.  So learning happens for the end-user or within the tools and systems they are building.  Learning that is distributed across all of these different strata is both exciting, and unpredictable.  What has been particularly interesting and exciting for me is to observe and begin to understand more about how agentic coding potentiates this, and how this kind of learning can be studied and harnessed.

I am enthusiastic to join the Anthropic Institute / Economics & Policy workstream.  My earliest research interests were in the anthropology of modern mathematics; I've had the opportunity to study that topic from AI, CSCW and HCI perspectives.  Economics and related practice-theoretic methods have been very informative, e.g., I drew on Benkler's Commons Based Peer Production in my work on paragogy, Elinor Ostrom's conception of institutions in my work on computational creativity, and Alexander-style design patterns in multiple applications.  More recently, I have been using these kinds of ideas "live" in my work with multiagent experiments with agentic coding systems; I'm particularly interested in Anthropic's exploration of "closing the loop in AI development" which is something I've been working on for several months from the end-user side.

I would like to show the reviewer my work on VSATARCS: documentation for the FUTON stack which condenses half a million lines of code virtual planetarium display: the point is not just that this is a pretty picture that makes complexity navigable, but that the image itself shows the kind of "constellational thinking" that makes the work possible in the first place.
What Closed-Loop AI Development tells us about the way to build human capability.
